companies.latest_signal: Core local commerce swung from a RMB2.0bn loss in Q1 2026 to a RMB5.7bn profit in Q2 2026 (7.9% margin) as delivery incentive spend eased — Q2 marketing expense grew only 11.5% vs 14.4% revenue growth — and Wang Xing told the call the price war 'did not create value for the industry'; New Initiatives operating loss also narrowed sequentially to RMB1.7bn.

companies.latest_signal: CEO Xu Ran told the Aug 13 2026 call that total food-delivery investment loss narrowed more than 50% YoY, with New Businesses segment loss down from RMB15.7bn (Q3 2025 peak) to RMB9.9bn in Q2 2026 as JD pulled back subsidy intensity; group operating profit turned positive on the back of the narrower new-business drag.

war_summary: Combined subsidy burn across the three hit roughly RMB150-173bn between mid-2025 and Q1 2026 (36Kr/Sina '外卖大战一年账单'), before SAMR's March 2026 signal via Economic Daily ('外卖大战该结束了') pushed platforms to dial back 'involution'-style competition. Meituan and JD both show clear, numerically-disclosed loss narrowing into H1 2026 — Meituan's core local commerce flipped from a RMB2.0bn loss to a RMB5.7bn profit and JD's new-business loss roughly halved from its Q3 2025 peak — while Alibaba remains the holdout, still spending to defend Taobao Flash Purchase's ~42-45% instant-retail share and no longer disclosing a hard EBITA loss figure, leaving it the one leg of the war not yet confirmed as narrowing in disclosed numbers even as management claims unit-economics are improving.
